name: Jyoti Solanki
conditions: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Vitamin D deficiency, vitamin B12 deficiency, heart failure with reduced ejection fraction. Patient reports fatigue, dyspnoea on exertion, occasional ankle swelling. Examination: BMI 27, BP 138/86, JVP not elevated, lungs clear, cardiac apex displaced laterally, mild pitting edema ankles. No wheeze. Smoking never. Plan: start cholecalciferol 60000 IU weekly for 8 weeks then 1000 IU OD; methylcobalamin 1500 mcg OD; sacubitril/valsartan 24/26 mg BD; bisoprolol 2.5 mg OD; spironolactone 25 mg OD; furosemide 40 mg OD; dapagliflozin 10 mg OD. Order baseline labs: 25‑OH vitamin D, calcium, phosphate; B12, MCV, Hb; electrolytes, creatinine, NT‑proBNP; echocardiogram.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Vitamin D deficiency improving, B12 normalising, HF stable. Symptoms: less fatigue, occasional mild dyspnoea on climbing stairs, no orthopnoea, ankle swelling unchanged. Exam: BP 130/82, JVP not raised, lungs clear, cardiac apex displaced laterally, trace ankle edema. Spirometry not indicated. Smoking never. Assessment: Vitamin D 22 ng/mL (still insufficient), B12 260 pg/mL, Hb 12.4 g/dL, NT‑proBNP 560 pg/mL. Plan: continue cholecalciferol 60000 IU weekly for remaining 4 weeks then switch to 1000 IU OD; continue methylcobalamin 1500 mcg OD; increase bisoprolol to 5 mg OD; continue other HF meds. Review in 8 weeks.

bisoprolol 5 mg OD
All other medications unchanged.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Transthoracic echocardiogram: Left ventricular ejection fraction 38% (ref ≥55%). Left ventricular end‑diastolic diameter 5.8 cm. Mild mitral regurgitation. No significant aortic stenosis. Right ventricular size normal. Inferior vena cava collapsibility >50% with sniff. NYHA class II.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Refer to Cardiology for optimisation of heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (EF 38%) and consideration of device therapy. Please review GDMT, assess eligibility for ICD/CRT‑D, and provide guidance on uptitration of beta‑blocker and ACE‑inhibitor/ARNi.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Cardiology opinion: Continue current ARNIsacubitril/valsartan, bisoprolol, spironolactone, furosemide, dapagliflozin. Recommend uptitrate bisoprolol to 10 mg OD as tolerated. No immediate indication for ICD; reassess in 3‑6 months. Lifestyle advice: fluid restriction 1.5 L/day, daily weights.

memories.author: patient
memories.text: Notice increased swelling in both ankles over past week, mild increase in breathlessness on walking to the mailbox. No chest pain. Using medications as prescribed.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Heart failure decompensation suspected. Symptoms: worsening ankle swelling, increased dyspnoea on mild exertion, occasional paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnoea. Exam: BP 128/80, JVP elevated to 4 cm, lungs with basilar crackles bilaterally, cardiac apex displaced laterally, pitting edema up to mid‑calf. Smoking never. Plan: increase furosemide to 60 mg OD, increase spironolactone to 50 mg OD, continue other HF meds, advise low‑salt diet, daily weights. Order electrolytes, creatinine, NT‑proBNP.

furosemide 60 mg OD
spironolactone 50 mg OD
All other medications unchanged.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Chest X‑ray: Cardiac silhouette mildly enlarged. Upper lobe vascular redistribution suggestive of mild pulmonary congestion. No pleural effusion. Lung fields otherwise clear.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Volume status improved after diuretic adjustment. Symptoms: reduced ankle swelling, dyspnoea only on brisk walk, orthopnoea absent. Exam: BP 130/78, JVP not elevated, lungs clear, trace ankle edema. Labs: K 4.8, creatinine 1.1, NT‑proBNP 480. Vitamin D now sufficient at 34 ng/mL. B12 stable at 300 pg/mL. Plan: stop high‑dose cholecalciferol, change to maintenance cholecalciferol 1000 IU OD; continue methylcobalamin 1500 mcg OD; reduce furosemide to 40 mg OD; keep spironolactone 25 mg OD; continue bisoprolol 5 mg OD (awaiting cardiology uptitration advice); continue sacubitril/valsartan, dapagliflozin. Review in 3 months.
